desert_p20_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_001.text: The printer's second map began with a broken corner. A worker had dropped the old relief block while clearing the bench, knocking the lower exchange symbol cleanly out of the edge. Du stared at the damage with an expression that made the worker begin apologising twice. Then he said the lost symbol needed replacing anyway. The worker stopped apologising and asked whether this meant the block could be used. Gao examined the remaining surface, found the main route clear enough for the present revision and asked for a dated replacement panel. Yue held the first proof to the window.

desert_p20_002.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_002.text: Its blank corner looked less certain than the old sheet had, and more accurate. The press room smelled of oil, damp paper and warmed wood. Sheets hung from lines above the workers' heads, each weighted so a gust through the shutters would not fold it into its neighbour. The rival publisher had brought a paper batch and a clerk to supervise his equal-release copies. Du's apprentice stood between them with the source list, refusing to let either senior man take the clean proof away before the captions were checked.

desert_p20_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_003.text: The printer wanted one finished instruction, not three customers leaning over the same block. He wiped his hands, rang a small desk bell and obtained silence by the simple method of being the person who actually owned the press.

desert_p20_004.speaker: du_she
desert_p20_004.text: This edition withdraws the plain freight symbol at the lower exchange and gives the currently observed ridge route. The old work roof is named as such. The valley's cart approach is dated and restricted under its responsible inspection, not treated as permanently open because our patient cart passed. Onion Hollow appears under its current community and district references. The well status belongs in a dated update panel. The relay's inner records remain partly unread. I know that is a great deal for one clean sheet. We can use the back.

desert_p20_005.speaker: du_she
desert_p20_005.text: My apprentice has threatened to use me as a paper weight if I say there is no room.

desert_p20_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_006.text: The rival clerk asked whether the back would be read. The apprentice said a numbered front instruction could direct the reader there. The printer suggested a small fold-out warning strip, cheap enough to replace when conditions changed. Gao liked the idea until its proposed type grew too small. Yue held the sample at an ordinary driver's reading distance. The load limit vanished into an elegant blur. They increased the strip's width and shortened the prose. The printer grumbled about paper waste and then cut a better proof.

desert_p20_007.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_007.text: A readable warning used more material than a decorative one, a cost the customers could either pay or decline with their names visible on the decision.

desert_p20_008.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p20_008.text: Do not make the date smaller than the turn. Both matter. The responsible route office may reopen or close a section after this sheet is printed, and a driver needs to know which observation he is holding. We can state the route authority's receiving point beside it. I am not asking you to print every field note. The exterior figure, correct origin and load warning belong on the front. The supporting source sequence can go on the back. If the lower paper class blurs the limit, use better paper for that strip.

desert_p20_009.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p20_009.text: Put its actual cost in the shared print estimate; I will sign it.

desert_p20_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_010.text: The printer's younger worker brought a tray of test impressions. One had the gate identifiers crisp, another the household label, a third neither because the pressure had been uneven. He asked Gao which mattered most. She said they needed both on the same impression. He looked vexed, then adjusted the packing beneath the block. Yue helped hang the rejected proofs where they could dry for inspection, marking each across the face so none could escape as a current map. The work was messy, repetitive in its physical motions and different in each result.

desert_p20_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_011.text: Ink made a stubborn little landscape on her fingernail. She could wash it later, when the sheet stopped failing. The rival representative wanted a more arresting title. The Valley Recovered, he proposed, would sell better than Present Route and Source Account. Du asked what had recovered. The well was still under clearance, the patient's leg still supported and the record sequence incomplete. The man said titles did not need to be clinical notes. He was right about that and wrong about this title. Gao suggested Roads Around Onion Hollow, with the current date large beneath it.

desert_p20_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_012.text: The representative considered the phrase and asked for a small exterior view. They agreed to an actual measured drawing, showing the court and restricted areas instead of a grand imaginary palace. The exterior artist arrived with a small portfolio and admitted that his first commission brief had described black glass floors. Du handed him the site drawing and said the glass belonged to a northern cabinet, while this relay had ordinary stone, wood and paper. The artist looked crestfallen, then interested in the high slit. He could draw its light without making it a doorway to another realm.

desert_p20_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_013.text: Gao asked him to include the damaged corner as it was. He objected that damage distracted the eye. Yue said distraction could be useful if it stopped a visitor standing under it. He smiled, accepted the point and put the unsafe corner where nobody could miss it.

desert_p20_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_014.text: At noon, Han brought the shared printing payment and a basket of cakes. The press worker wanted to wash before eating; the senior customers wanted to keep discussing titles. Han put the basket on the clean table and invited the people who had been working with ink to take their break first. The customers followed when they realised cake would not wait for their conclusion. Du's apprentice selected a piece with an unbroken sesame crust and looked at Yue's stained finger. Yue said the map had bitten her.

desert_p20_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_015.text: The apprentice replied that maps mostly bit readers, so a contributor might take her turn. They laughed and ate in the brief mercy of a room without proofs in their hands.

desert_p20_016.speaker: han_xun
desert_p20_016.text: The print run is paid for under the correction allocation. Extra replacement strips will be held at both map offices and the receiving yard, so a driver need not buy a whole fresh atlas to obtain today's warning. We have the circulation list from both presses. The old cards should be marked withdrawn where the subscribers can actually see it. I cannot find every second-hand buyer. I can put the notice where those buyers ask for a hire and make my own clerks give it before they praise a shortcut. My daughter has volunteered to check whether they do.

desert_p20_017.speaker: han_xun
desert_p20_017.text: I advise them to take that seriously.

desert_p20_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_018.text: The printer asked whether Han's daughter needed employment. Han said she already had plans involving teaching and a household that would object to losing all her mornings. The printer wanted a literate temporary checker for the warning strips. She was offered a bounded paid task after her own schedule was consulted, not recruited through her father's proud anecdote. Han carried the offer home at lunch and let her answer it. She accepted two afternoons, with the rate and work written down. Yue saw her arrive later wearing a plain apron and carrying the enormous flower drawing only in memory.

desert_p20_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_019.text: At the press, she wanted to be judged by whether a driver could read the date.

desert_p20_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_020.text: The well clearance report reached the press room during the second afternoon. After the cover repair, controlled flushing, lining checks and the responsible source review, the fresh draw met the applicable reopening conditions on repeated examinations. The community keeper witnessed the source work and signed the actual reopening date. The report did not call boiling a cure for uncertain minerals, nor declare the well incapable of future trouble. Its maintenance and observation plan remained attached. Bao reviewed the clinical-use conditions with the water officer. Gao changed the update strip before the main run.

desert_p20_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_021.text: The well was reopening because a sequence of work had succeeded, not because the town was tired of a closure notice.

desert_p20_022.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_022.text: Yue took the news to the older patient. The woman closed her eyes and asked someone to read the date again. Her daughter did, slowly. The niece said the sleeping jars could return to being reserve vessels. The patient said they would still need cleaning, which reduced the room's triumph to a scale everyone recognised. Bao explained the source clearance was current and conditional on continued maintenance. The woman nodded impatiently; she knew wells did not survive by applause. Then she looked at Yue and asked whether the keeper had received the rope. He had, with a signed invoice.

desert_p20_023.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_023.text: She smiled more broadly at that. Some parts of good news could be held in a hand. The reopened well did not erase the household claim. The family still requested the unfinished old balance reviewed, and the community still wanted its source work named in the public account. Du's apprentice had placed the historical contribution explanation on the map's back, omitting private balances while keeping the existence of the living enquiry. The older patient read the wording and changed one term from subscribers to households. Her grandmother had never subscribed to a map. Yue carried the correction back.

desert_p20_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_024.text: Du accepted it without defending the neatness of his original phrase. A word could be inaccurate simply by belonging too comfortably to the room where it had been written.

desert_p20_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_025.text: Tuo visited the press after her permitted walk. She inspected the current footpath label and the village approach, then found a dotted line that still resembled an invitation to loaded traffic. Gao said it marked a historical connection. Tuo asked what a tired driver would think at dusk. They changed the line style and moved the explanation nearer. The apprentice gave Tuo a chair before the guide's ankle began to protest. Tuo thanked her and sat without pretending it was for someone else. Du watched the exchange with an affection he did not try to improve into a comment.

desert_p20_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_026.text: People were learning to keep one another useful without making usefulness expensive to endure.

desert_p20_027.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p20_027.text: The public ridge should look more ordinary than the shorter turning ground. Drivers love a line that seems to save them effort, and a pretty line can bully a warning. I know because I have followed pretty lines and then blamed their maker for my own hurry. Give the ridge its landmarks and decent space. Give the restricted section its actual restriction. We can print the old winter shelter as historical, but do not put a fresh roof on it in the artist's view. A traveller should not arrive expecting tea because the picture wanted a balanced composition.

desert_p20_028.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p20_028.text: The weather will not admire your composition either.

desert_p20_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_029.text: The artist overheard and erased a roof beam he had restored by imagination. He said Tuo had a gift for making picturesque work less comfortable. She said she charged for that gift when properly hired. He offered to pay for a brief route-picture review and she accepted after checking the small task against her recovery schedule. Their agreement occupied a corner of the apprentice's notebook. Du looked pleased that a guide's practical reading could be work beside the surveyor's measurements. Yue held the finished exterior drawing up to the light.

desert_p20_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_030.text: It looked like a place where people might actually decide where to stand, which gave it a beauty the invented beam had lacked.

desert_p20_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_031.text: The responsible route crew completed the wider approach repair while the paper run was being prepared. Their current inspection released the restored cart line within the registered wagon limits, with the lower footbridge still closed pending its own work. The emergency support and former nine-hundred-and-fifty restriction were superseded only by that dated repair and assessment, not by the successful evacuation alone. Gao added the actual notice to the source packet and checked the new departure plan against it. The return conservation visit could now be considered on its proper loads.

desert_p20_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_032.text: A repaired cart path did not open the damaged foot crossing by association. The map would show both states separately. The funded return team consisted of six adults: Gao, Du, the independent conservator, the mason and two contracted drivers, with four mules and two inspected carts. Lin, Tuo and Bao would remain in town. Its six-day plan allowed two working days at the relay between travel, with one delay day possible before the protected essentials became the likely source. The team purchased one thousand usable litres of clean municipal water, including two protected hundreds, within the assigned tank capacities.

desert_p20_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_033.text: Its ordinary daily forecast was one hundred and two for people and animals together. The stock, fodder, food, fuel, custody materials and fees belonged to a separate funded visit, not leftovers wished out of the former expedition. The two drivers confirmed their terms before the new visit was signed. The municipal driver obtained paid leave covering the actual schedule and return contingency; his school-counter arrangements would wait for the stated date rather than become another promise squeezed between journeys. The other driver's wife accepted the renewed departure after the direct arrival notes and employer terms were shown.

desert_p20_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_034.text: Neither household had acquired a duty to tolerate indefinite silence. Han reserved the filling window, checked the inspected carts and paid the return provision into the receiving house. He would again remain home. His daughter watched the signatures and made no joke about flowers. This work had become serious enough for ordinary trust.

desert_p20_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_035.text: The conservation scope permitted supported handling and a documented transfer only where condition and access allowed it, with the community's receipts and current interests represented. It did not authorise private sale of old pages. The conservator selected more suitable support and transport materials after the first visit's condition record, still bounded by cart loads and return needs. The mason would reassess the room on arrival. Gao wanted the drainage grades; Du wanted the missing sequence; both agreed the professional condition decision could end the handling.

desert_p20_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_036.text: Yue listened at the preparation table and recognised a plan built from what had actually happened. The first interrupted visit had not been wasted merely because it needed a second. Du invited Yue to join, then remembered the settled crew count before she answered. He apologised for asking as if one more companion weighed nothing. She said she appreciated the thought and would remain in town this time. The patients' accessible lodging enquiry still needed ordinary errands, and she wanted days in which she chose her own pace. She was not taking a permanent care post. Du accepted that distinction.

desert_p20_037.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_037.text: He asked her to keep the apprentice from treating every late proof as a private disaster. Yue said the apprentice could speak for herself, and Du laughed at the familiar shape of the correction. He wished her several good quiet days without attaching work to them. The apprentice did speak for herself. She wanted authority to release the paid warning strips while Du was away, under the checked text and stated date policy, and she wanted her working hours respected. He granted the bounded release authority and put it in the office book.

desert_p20_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_038.text: The rival clerk received the same corrected source text without obtaining control over her desk. Han's daughter would finish her two paid checking afternoons and leave. The room's future work acquired enough names and times that it no longer depended on Du rushing back before anyone could make a decision. He seemed both proud and faintly bereaved. His apprentice handed him the travel folder before he could linger.

desert_p20_039.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_039.text: Bao visited the new filling with Gao to review the source record, though she would not travel. The municipal keeper measured two five-hundred-litre stocks into the clean assigned tanks, protected compartments included. The receiving totals matched the team's thousand usable litres. Thirty kilograms of cooking fuel and the counted food and animal provision were loaded under the separate manifest. Bao checked the medical basics the drivers would carry and the real transfer contacts along their route. She was not sending a remote clinic by writing a telephone-like promise nobody could use.

desert_p20_040.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_040.text: She left them clear instructions and qualified destinations for actual problems. Gao thanked her and checked the ordinary first-day forecast one last time.

desert_p20_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_041.text: The morning of departure found Yue at the Black Gate with Tuo and Han's daughter. Gao stood beside the first cart, wearing the blue-grey coat with its old dust finally washed out. Du's folder held the transfer numbers and source copies; the conservator's prepared carrier held empty supports waiting for whatever condition allowed. The mason checked the last strap without making a ceremony of it. The six adults and four mules left under the funded term. Lin watched until the road hid the wheel tops. She had expected staying behind to feel like missing the real novel.

desert_p20_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_042.text: Instead it felt like the beginning of a chapter in which town could be more than a place to recover between departures.

desert_p20_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_043.text: At the press, the second map came off the block after the travellers left. Han's daughter read its front at the same distance used in the proofs. The date, correct origins, current route conditions and receiving point were clear. Du's apprentice checked the source back and counted the first released bundles against the paid circulation list. The rival clerk signed his equal copies. Yue held one ordinary paper-class sheet and could find the ridge without pretending the valley was empty. The map had no perfect corner.

desert_p20_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_044.text: The replacement panel left a visible join, a small scar showing where new knowledge had been fitted into old work. The printer wanted to hide that join in the next run. The apprentice said it could be neater once the text was stable, but the visible date panel should remain replaceable. He agreed, interested now in the practical manufacturing problem. Yue asked him whether the map was finally finished. He said the paid run was finished; the road would decide how long its conditions lasted.

desert_p20_045.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_045.text: Then he asked her to stop philosophical questions and carry the dry sheets to the counting table. She complied, smiling. It was a light ordinary task within her hands' recovery, and the sheets made a soft continuous sound against one another. An honest map could still be sold, folded and taken to work. The first subscriber to collect a replacement was a carter who had bought the rival card second-hand. He had no original subscription number and expected to be refused. Han's correction notice at the receiving yard had directed him to the free current warning strip.

desert_p20_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_046.text: The apprentice gave it to him and marked the withdrawn card plainly in his presence. He could keep the old paper as a record; he should use the current restriction. The carter read it, asked one turn question and left satisfied. The rival clerk looked thoughtful. Distribution to actual readers was more awkward than mailing neat customer lists, and more effective than arguing that second-hand buyers belonged to nobody.

desert_p20_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_047.text: Yue took a map to the shoemaker's stall. The girl found Onion Hollow at once because she had a flower from there. She found the north exchange next and asked why the different places had once been confused. Yue showed the separate origins and scale notes. The girl followed the lines with an ink-free finger, then asked where someone could sit if a leg hurt. That question was not on the route sheet. Yue pointed to the village resting yard in her own notebook and explained that travellers should ask its current keeper rather than expect a permanent free bed.

desert_p20_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_048.text: The girl said maps ought to have an attached person. Yue said many good ones almost did.

desert_p20_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_049.text: In the rented courtyard that evening, the map lay beside Yue's bowl rather than above it as an instruction to leave. The shopkeeper's daughter admired the exterior view and asked whether the room's high slit really made that shape of light. Yue said the drawing used the observed time and position, with damaged areas shown. The girl thought the missing roof corner made it less like a palace and more like a place somebody could repair. Yue agreed. Beyond the room, the town settled into ordinary evening trades. The six-person conservation team was somewhere on its actual road.

desert_p20_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_050.text: Here, the second map had already begun another journey, moving from a paid press into readers' hands.

desert_p20_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_051.text: On the first afternoon of Du's absence, the apprentice found that one bundle had been tied with the warning strips facing inward. A subscriber would have to untie everything before reading the date. She called the packer back, untied the bundle herself and showed the outside label position. He said the old method was faster. She asked him to time both methods with the printer's watch. The difference was small, and the outward label did its job. Han's daughter stood nearby counting proofs, trying not to grin.

desert_p20_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_052.text: When the packer finally tied the new bundle, she marked its count and carried it to the released stack. The twine sat neatly beneath the visible date. The rival clerk stayed late because his office wanted one more attractive cover impression. The apprentice offered the paid exterior view already agreed and refused an invented clear roof. He sent a runner to obtain the office's answer. The runner came back tired and cross, with acceptance written on the proof. Yue gave him water from the press room's ordinary town supply after the printer offered it.

desert_p20_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_053.text: The boy drank, wiped his mouth and asked why customers always found their last opinion after the shutters were half closed. The printer said that was how one recognised a customer.

desert_p20_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_054.text: Yue and the apprentice ate a late meal beside the counting table. The apprentice wanted her own small publishing room someday, perhaps one that made practical household guides as well as maps. She did not want to inherit every drawer in Du's office merely because he had grown used to her knowing what was inside. Yue asked whether he knew that. The apprentice said he knew she wanted a room; he still assumed it would be a room upstairs. She was preparing to tell him the rest after the conservation return.

desert_p20_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_055.text: Outside, a cart wheel caught a stone and bumped past the shutters. The table shook, and both women instinctively moved their bowls away from the proofs.

desert_p20_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_056.text: At Han's receiving yard, the second map acquired its first greasy thumbprint. A flour carter held the date strip while eating fried dough, then apologised when he saw the mark. Han said the sheet could survive being used, provided the warning remained legible. He gave the man a clean wrapper for the rest and asked him to read the relevant turn aloud. The carter got it right. Yue liked the thumbprint. It marked the paper's escape from the desk more clearly than a release seal.

desert_p20_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_057.text: The carter folded the map into his coat and climbed into his waiting wagon, wiping the remaining oil on a rag already beyond redemption.

desert_p20_058.speaker: han_xun
desert_p20_058.text: I used to imagine a dependable firm as one that never admitted trouble where a customer could hear it. Then a driver asked me whether the collar would come out of his wages, and I heard what that kind of dependability sounded like from the wrong end. I still want customers to trust us. I also want the driver to bring me the loose brace before it becomes expensive. My daughter says I have become tiresome about service notes. I say she has become tiresome about type size.

desert_p20_059.speaker: han_xun
desert_p20_059.text: We have agreed that neither of us is to stop, which may be a mistake for everyone else in the house.

desert_p20_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_060.text: The firm had actually revised its service interval for concealed tank fittings after the workshop finding. Comparable mounts were opened and examined under the new schedule; one worn seat was replaced before hire, with no accident required to justify it. Han showed Yue the paid workshop entry rather than merely describe a change of heart. The old second-cart driver came to collect his family bird from the carpenter and inspected the repaired seat on his assigned wagon. He gave it a small pleased nod. His daughter would probably care more about the bird's tail.

desert_p20_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_061.text: He packed the wooden gift carefully and went home with two repairs completed, one much easier to show a child.

desert_p20_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_062.text: Bao's proposed treatment-room attendant arrived for the first ordinary cleaning instruction. She had worked in a tea stall and knew how to keep surfaces clean without yet knowing a clinic's receiving sequence. Bao started with storage, hands and the distinction between taking a person's name and giving medical advice. Yue helped label the plain shelves at the town preparation room, a paid short task from the pilot budget. The attendant asked whether she would wear a white coat. Bao said her own clean practical clothes were sufficient; she would be introduced by her actual role.

desert_p20_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_063.text: The woman looked relieved and brought out a notebook with an immaculate new wrapper.

desert_p20_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_064.text: The town clinic social clerk inspected an accessible courtyard house two lanes from the ward. Its owner had three ground-level rooms around a paved open court, a wide gate and a shaded passage without stairs. One room was already vacant after a merchant moved his office. The others could be used by the patient and companion under a short lease if the wash arrangement and doorway threshold were adjusted. The owner wanted reliable rent and no damage to the old stone drain. The family wanted a room where the supported leg could rest and visitors need not become porters.

desert_p20_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_065.text: Yue accompanied the permitted inspection carrying the measuring sheet, then watched the clerk test the door's clear width. The older woman's daughter could pay part of the short lease, the household a further share and the district emergency accommodation provision the balance for its approved initial term. Longer recovery support would be reviewed before that term expired. The arrangement did not consume the disputed historic contribution or make its outcome a condition of present care. The niece asked whether she could stay as companion while doing limited paid work elsewhere after clearance.

desert_p20_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_066.text: The owner agreed within the occupancy limit and ordinary house rules. The clerk wrote the names and review date on the draft. The court smelled of wet stone where a neighbour had just washed the paving.

desert_p20_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_067.text: The patient heard the proposal from the clerk and daughter together. She asked to see a drawing of the courtyard before agreeing to a room she could not yet visit. Yue drew the wide door, low bed place and shaded bench from the actual inspection, without putting a flower in every empty corner. The woman approved of the plainness and asked whether the view contained a wall. It did, but also a strip of court and a little tree. She said that would do. The clinic would decide when she could transfer under its care plan.

desert_p20_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_068.text: For now the draft lease stayed unsigned by the owner until the family confirmed the actual receiving date. The niece wanted to carry her aunt's bedding from home. Bao asked who would fetch it and how its weight would reach town. The household had a scheduled market wagon with paid space available; the keeper could send a defined bundle and retain the receipt. The niece did not need to walk a whole desert road with a load her shoulder had been told to avoid. She made the list and sent it through the known carrier.

desert_p20_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_069.text: Yue watched her cross out a large blanket and choose the lighter one appropriate to the warm room. The pencil marks looked like ordinary domestic work. They were also part of the injury's recovery.

desert_p20_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_070.text: The young worker's medical recheck allowed more ordinary hand use while preserving limits on dirty heavy tasks until the cut finished healing. He sat the school's basic reading assessment with the bandage reduced and an examiner who cared chiefly whether he understood the instruction. He did. The practical entry task would come later under safe conditions. His grant application remained pending, and he would not tell the aunt he had a place yet. He left the room holding the result slip against his chest for a moment before folding it.

desert_p20_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_071.text: Yue saw him outside the gate and asked whether he wanted a bun. He said yes, with the shy decisiveness of somebody suddenly hungry. They ate beside the school's little court, where a trainee had left a line of rejected latch plates on a sill. The worker looked at them and asked whether failures were always displayed. A teacher passing nearby said only the useful ones. He had been taught to hide every bad repair from visitors, which was part pride and part fear of losing work. The teacher picked up one plate and explained its uneven seat.

desert_p20_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_072.text: The young man listened without pretending he already knew. Yue left the conversation when they no longer needed her to make it begin. She could hear the teacher's low voice behind her, followed by a careful question and the scrape of metal against stone.

desert_p20_073.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_073.text: The onion flower on the shoemaker's counter began to dry more brittle than its maker had intended. The girl made a small support for it from discarded thin wood and tied the stem without crushing it. She asked Yue whether preserving a thing changed it. Yue said the conservator would probably ask what change and why. The girl decided that was a satisfactory answer because the flower now stood instead of leaning against the stone fish. Her father looked at the support, smiled, and handed her another scrap for the next repair.

desert_p20_074.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_074.text: Yue paid for a new lace she actually needed and left with its plain durability folded in her pocket. That evening Han's daughter completed her second paid checking shift. The printer counted the accepted sheets, paid her stated fee and offered further work if she wanted it. She thanked him and declined the next week because of her teaching course. Han collected her at the gate and visibly resisted explaining the refusal for her. She did not need him to.

desert_p20_075.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_075.text: Yue walked with them through the market, hearing the daughter describe how one blurred date had taken more work than a whole border ornament. Han asked whether the ornament had been attractive. She said extremely, which was why it had annoyed her. They bought a pot of basil for the household and carried it carefully between them.

desert_p20_076.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_076.text: At home the older basil had survived Han's renewed watering schedule. His mother inspected the new pot and warned him that two plants did not make an orchard. He said neither had made a freight firm, yet everyone continued giving him responsibilities. The daughter put her print fee in her own course purse and pinned the clean proof on the wall beside the flower wheel. Han's mother could read the large date from her chair and declared the map finally suitable for people with sensible eyes. Yue ate supper with them and said very little.

desert_p20_077.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_077.text: The room needed no report from her to justify her place at its table.

desert_p20_078.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_078.text: The conservation team's first arrival message reached town by the ordinary quarry dispatch the next day. Six adults and four mules had reached their planned receiving point; the restored cart approach would be checked again before use, and the current well source had reopened under its officer's record. Their travelling stock had lost only its actual draws, with no community water added. Gao listed the source and weather references for the visit. Du added a line for his apprentice about the missing folder she had packed correctly after all.

desert_p20_079.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_079.text: She read it, smiled at his inability to admit surprise gracefully, and filed the message beneath the paid office schedule. Tuo came for the message and stayed to review a public question from a travelling merchant. The merchant wanted to know whether reopened meant he could send a heavy wagon to any part of the valley. She showed him the restored cart approach notice and the still closed footbridge. Different structures had different conditions. He began to complain about complicated maps. Tuo asked what load he actually wished to carry and where.

desert_p20_080.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_080.text: Once he answered, the route office's current limit could be applied without philosophy. He left with the right instruction and the guide's modest paid consultation receipt. She sat down afterwards, pleased with the work and unwilling to walk another unnecessary street to celebrate it.

desert_p20_081.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_081.text: Yue spent her free morning mending the notebook wrapper. She had copied too many temporary sheets into it to keep treating the old binding as a miracle. The stationer sold her thread and showed a simple reinforcement that did not require professional conservation. The new stitches were ordinary, slightly uneven and entirely her own. She placed the stage-five practice notes apart from the caravan figures, so neither would masquerade as the other's qualification. Outside the window, the neighbour's cat walked the washing line support with outrageous confidence. It landed beside her work and demanded attention.

desert_p20_082.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_082.text: She gave it a hand for one minute, then moved the thread out of its paw's reach.

desert_p20_083.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_083.text: The courtyard landlord accepted the family terms after the clinic proposed a likely transfer date subject to the next examination. He booked an ordinary low town cart and a qualified escort through the clinic's arranged service, with its actual fee included in the initial plan. The doorway threshold would be fitted with a stable small ramp by a local carpenter, its width and support checked before the patient arrived. The daughter inspected the wash corner and chose where a chair could stand without narrowing the path. Yue carried the signed duplicate to the niece.

desert_p20_084.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_084.text: The girl read the date twice, then looked toward her aunt's bed. There would soon be a room in which neither of them was merely waiting for the next ward round. The older patient asked whether the courtyard tree produced fruit. The landlord's drawing showed only leaves, and Yue did not invent an answer. The daughter went to ask. It produced small bitter plums the neighbours mostly ignored. The patient said she had once made excellent preserve from bitter plums and immediately began assigning pots that did not yet exist. Her niece stopped the assignment after the first pot.

desert_p20_085.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_085.text: They would inspect the room before organising its whole harvest. The woman grumbled, then laughed. The future had reappeared in a ridiculous domestic form, involving fruit too sour to eat and a leg still resting under support.

desert_p20_086.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_086.text: On the last evening before the planned courtyard preparations, Yue passed the press window and saw the second map hanging among ordinary work: price lists, household notices and a school term sheet. It no longer occupied the room as a singular revelation. Drivers were folding it into coats; offices were replacing date strips; families were finding their own names on the supporting account. The press worker closed the shutters and called good night. Yue answered and walked on.

desert_p20_087.speaker: narrator
desert_p20_087.text: The old relay remained a place for funded work, the valley a place where people lived, and town a place with a courtyard about to receive someone who needed a room with a wide door.
